hints: Focus on the type of addition here, HBr adding across a C=C double bond follows Markovnikov's rule for the major product.
Draw out 3-ethylhex-3-ene, C3 has two alkyl groups and no H, while C4 has one H, so H from HBr goes to C4 and Br goes to C3.
Now name the alkane product carefully, Br and the ethyl group are both on the same carbon, and choose the numbering that gives the lowest locants.
walkthrough:
**Draw the starting alkene**

Think of the double bond as the reactive spot. 3-ethylhex-3-ene is:

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}(\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3)=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

Notice C3 is joined to two ethyl groups with no H, while C4 is joined to one H.

**Apply Markovnikov addition of HBr**

Remember, H adds to the C with more H atoms, and Br adds to the more stable carbocation position.

$$\text{C}=\text{C} + \text{HBr} \rightarrow \text{CH} + \text{C-Br}$$

So H adds to C4 and Br adds to the more substituted tertiary C3 to give $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C(Br)(CH}_2\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

**Name the product with lowest numbers**

Both the bromo and the ethyl substituents are now on carbon 3 of a hexane chain.

This gives 3-bromo-3-ethylhexane directly, with no need to renumber from the other end.

options.A: Correct. Br adds to the more substituted C3 to form a tertiary carbocation intermediate, giving $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C(Br)(Et)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Numbered from the nearest end this is 3-bromo-3-ethylhexane, which uses the lowest possible locants.
options.B: Incorrect. This is the correct IUPAC name for the anti-Markovnikov product where Br ends up on C4. The major product puts Br on the more stable tertiary position C3, not C4.
options.C: Incorrect. This describes the same connectivity as the anti-Markovnikov product (Br on one carbon, ethyl on the adjacent carbon) but numbered the wrong way round. It is wrong both in regiochemistry and in numbering, since bromo should get the lower number.
options.D: Incorrect. This describes the correct connectivity (Br and ethyl on the same carbon) but numbered from the wrong end of the chain. IUPAC rules require the lowest locants, so 3,3 is preferred over 4,4.
